Convert contMap(s) of a continuous trait into simmap(s) with discrete states

Source: R/convert_contMap_to_simmap.R
convert_contMap_to_simmap.Rd

Converts the continuous trait history(ies) mapped on a phylogeny into a stochastic character map of class "simmap" with discrete states obtained by cutting the trait values into bins (e.g., "low", "medium", "high").

The output can be used as a simmap in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to constrain the grafting of missing taxa by the continuous trait (e.g., a taxon known to have a high body size can only be grafted on branches in the "high" state).

The function accepts a single contMap, typically built with phytools::contMap(), or a list of contMaps typically obtained from continuous stochastic mapping approach such as the one featured in the contsimmap R package. A single contMap gives a single simmap. A list of contMaps, typically covering the uncertainty of the reconstruction (e.g., one contMap per stochastic history of a continuous trait), gives a multiSimmap, with one simmap per contMap.

Usage

convert_contMap_to_simmap(
  contMap,
  breaks = NULL,
  n_bins = NULL,
  probs = NULL,
  states,
  tip_values = NULL,
  min_segment_proportion = 0.01,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

contMap

An object of class "contMap", or a list of such objects. All the contMaps of a list must be built on the same phylogeny (same tips, topology, branch lengths and order of the edges). A list is named after the names of the contMaps, with map_1, map_2, ... if no names are provided.

breaks

Numeric vector. The interior cut points between the bins, in the units of the trait. Values lower than the first cut point belong to the first state, and so on. They must be provided in increasing order, be different values, and lie within the range of the trait values (see Details). If not, a warning is sent and the cut points are sorted and/or the duplicated values removed. Exactly one of breaks, n_bins and probs arguments must be provided.

n_bins

Integer, at least 2. The number of bins of equal width over the range of the trait values at the tips. Exactly one of breaks, n_bins and probs arguments must be provided.

probs

Numeric vector with values strictly between 0 and 1. The quantile levels, computed on the trait values observed at the tips, at which to cut the bins. They must be provided in increasing order and be different values, otherwise a warning is sent and they are sorted and/or the duplicated values removed (e.g., c(1/3, 2/3) for three bins of equal numbers of tips). Exactly one of breaks, n_bins and probs arguments must be provided.

states

Character vector. The names of the states, from the bin with the lowest values to the bin with the highest values. Its length must match the number of bins: the number of interior cut points + 1.

tip_values

Numeric vector (optional). The observed trait values at the tips, named after the tips of the phylogeny (or provided in the order of the tips if unnamed). If provided, they are used instead of the values read from the contMap(s) to compute the cut points (n_bins and probs) and to set the state of each tip (the last segment of each terminal branch), so that the tips are in the state of their observed value. The same values are used for all the contMaps of a list. They must lie within the range of the trait values of the contMap(s). If NULL, the tip values are read from the contMap(s), where they are only approximated (see Details).

min_segment_proportion

Numeric between 0 (included) and 1 (excluded). The minimum duration of a segment of a branch, as a proportion of the depth of the tree (root age). Default is 0.01. Shorter segments are merged into their longest neighbour on the branch (see Details for why this may matter). Use 0 to keep every crossing of a cut point.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print the progress of the conversion (every 10% of the contMaps) when a list of several contMaps is provided. Default is TRUE.

Value

Depending on the nature of the input:

  • If contMap is a single contMap: an object of class "simmap".

  • If contMap is a list of contMaps: an object of class "multiSimmap" in which each element is a "simmap" ordered to match the initial contMaps.

The interior cut points used to discretize the trait values are stored in the attribute "breaks" of the output, and the names of the states (from the lowest to the highest values) in its attribute "states". They allow to convert other values, e.g., the trait values of the missing taxa, into the same states with phylograftR::convert_values_to_states().

Details

Principle

A contMap stores the trait history as a series of short segments along each branch, with ancestral node values typically estimated from a maximum likelihood reconstruction under a Brownian motion (BM) model and linearly interpolated along the branches.

During discretization, each segment is assigned to the bin its value falls in, and consecutive segments of the same bin are merged. A value equal to a cut point belongs to the bin above it. The result is a simmap (as in phytools::make.simmap()) where the states are the bins.

Cutting the trait values

Provide exactly one of the three arguments:

  • breaks: the cut points are chosen by the user.

  • n_bins: uses bins of equal width over the range of the tip values.

  • probs: uses bins defined by quantiles of the tip values.

n_bins and probs are computed on the tip values (averaged across the contMaps of a list). By default, they are read from the contMaps, which store the trait values on a finite scale of colors (from 0 to 1000 in phytools::contMap()), so they approximate the observed data. Provide the observed values with tip_values to use them instead (see below).

Tip values

A contMap stores the trait history as a series of short segments along each branch, with the value of each segment interpolated from the estimated values at the nodes. The value associated to a segment is a single value for the whole segment, on a finite scale of colors. As a result, the value of the last segment of a terminal branch is nearly, but not identical to the observed value at the tip. With the default settings, the function extrapolates the tip value from the last segments, which is only an approximate. The difference is usually small compared to the range of the trait, but it can move the tip of a taxon with a value close to a cut point into the neighboring state, or shift the cut points obtained from n_bins or probs.

To avoid this, provide the observed tip values with tip_values: they are then used to compute the cut points, and each tip is set in the state of its observed value, so that the tips of the simmaps are in the same states as the observed data converted with phylograftR::convert_values_to_states(). This is recommended whenever the tip data used to build the contMap(s) are available. When the observed state of a tip differs from the state of the interpolated segments just before it, the terminal branch ends with a short segment in the state of the observed value (the segment at the tip is never merged away, see min_segment_proportion).

The values of the internal branches are reconstructed and are expected to shrink towards the intermediate values under a BM process (or towards one specific direction if a directional model was used to fit the contMaps), because ancestral values are averaged over their descendants. As a consequence, bins defined from the tips will contain a smaller share of the internal branches for the extreme states than for the intermediate states.

breaks must be interior cut points: they must lie within the range of the trait values, i.e., between the minimum and the maximum of the values of all the contMaps. A cut point beyond this range is an error. A cut point equal to the minimum or the maximum is ignored with a warning, because it would define an empty bin.

The cut points must be in increasing order and different values. This is checked for the three arguments, including the cut points derived from n_bins and probs (e.g., many tips sharing the same value can give identical quantiles). Unsorted cut points are sorted, and duplicated values are removed, with an informative warning.

The number of states must be equal to the number of bins (the number of cut points + 1, after the cut points equal to the boundaries were ignored). Removing cut points reduces the number of bins, so states must match the number of bins left.

Short segments

When using contMaps derived from continuous stochastic mapping processes such as the one featured in the contsimmap R package, trait values can wander around a cut point: the trait evolutionary history can crosses the threshold several times over short distances, resulting in tiny segments alternating states. Segments shorter than min_segment_proportion times the depth of the tree are merged, from the shortest to the longest, into their longest neighbour on the same branch. A branch shorter than the minimum length gets a single state: the one with the longest total duration, or the state of the tip for a terminal branch. On a terminal branch, the segment at the tip is never merged away to ensure tip states matched with observed tip data. Setting min_segment_proportion = 0 keeps all the crossings.

This is not an issue for contMap featuring linear interpolation of ancestral trait values as in phytools::contMap(), since trait values can only vary monotonously along branches (i.e., decrease, increase, or remain stable, but not a combination of two), thus cannot cross each cut point multiple times.

Cautions for interpretation

  • The resulting simmaps is/are a discretization of the reconstructed trait to constrain the grafting of missing taxa. It is not a stochastic map of a discrete trait: the number of transitions depends on the resolution of the contMap and on min_segment_proportion and should not be interpreted as a rate of evolution of discrete states.

  • Nodes with reconstructed values close to a cut point have uncertain states. Providing a list of contMaps covering the uncertainty (see below) is the way to account for it, as each grafted phylogeny can then use a different simmap.

  • The states depend on the cut points. A taxon whose allowed states are defined by a threshold can have different eligible branches if the threshold is moved. Ideally, you would want to compare several sets of cut points before relying on the results (see vignette("continuous_data")).

  • As for the use of simmap derived from discrete states, constraining the grafting by a trait that will then be analyzed (e.g., the association of the trait with diversification) biases the results towards the constraint. Interpret such analyses accordingly.

Accounting for uncertainty in trait estimates: continuous stochastic mapping

A single contMap is a point estimate. To cover the uncertainty of the reconstruction, provide a list of contMaps, each one built from one possible history of the trait. For example, the contsimmap R package samples histories of a continuous trait on a phylogeny, and the function deepSTRAPP::convert_contsimmap_to_contMaps() converts them into a list of contMaps (see Examples). The output of this function is then a multiSimmap, that can be used in the grafting functions like any multiSimmap, to account for uncertainty in the ancestral trait reconstructions.

The function deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data() is the recommended way to obtain such a list of contMaps: with run_stochastic_maps = TRUE, it fits the evolutionary model(s) (selected by AICc), runs the continuous stochastic mapping with contsimmap::make.contsimmap() and converts the maps into contMaps in a single call, with additional options to fine-tune the process (see Examples). The example below uses contsimmap directly to credit the authors of the continuous stochastic mapping approach and to show the steps usde internally by deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data().

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::convert_values_to_states() to convert continuous values of the missing taxa into the states of the simmap.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades, using the states to constrain the grafting.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades, using the states to constrain the grafting.
